theory.intro: Scientific notation makes numbers easy to compare: the power of $10$ sets the size, so the powers are compared first and the coefficients only break a tie.
facts: The power of $10$ dominates: $1.4 \times 10^{5}$ is larger than $9.6 \times 10^{4}$, even though $9.6 > 1.4$.
For negative powers, the power closer to zero is larger: $10^{-3} > 10^{-5}$, so $2 \times 10^{-3} > 8 \times 10^{-5}$.
Only when the powers are equal do the coefficients decide the order.
A number that is not in scientific notation (a decimal, or a coefficient outside $1 \le a < 10$) should be rewritten as $a \times 10^{n}$ before comparing.
steps: Write any number that is not in scientific notation in the form $a \times 10^{n}$.
Compare the powers of 10 — the number with the higher power is larger.
If the powers are equal, compare the coefficients.

foundation.solution_text:
The powers differ, so compare them first: $10^{6} > 10^{4}$.
$3.2 \times 10^{6}$ is larger.

The powers are equal, so compare the coefficients: $5.8 > 5.1$.
$5.8 \times 10^{3}$ is larger.

The coefficients are equal, so compare the powers: $-2 > -6$.
$2.4 \times 10^{-2}$ is larger.

Compare the powers first: $-4 < -3$, so $10^{-4} < 10^{-3}$.
$6.5 \times 10^{-4}$ is smaller.

The powers are all different, so they set the order: $10^{1} < 10^{2} < 10^{3}$.
$9.9 \times 10^{1},\ 4.7 \times 10^{2},\ 1.2 \times 10^{3}$

The coefficients are equal, so the powers set the order: $-8 < -5 < -3$.
$3.5 \times 10^{-8},\ 3.5 \times 10^{-5},\ 3.5 \times 10^{-3}$

development.solution_text:
$0.000\,83 = 8.3 \times 10^{-4}$
The powers are equal, so compare the coefficients: $8.6 > 8.3$.
$8.6 \times 10^{-4}$ is larger.

$45\,000 = 4.5 \times 10^{4}$
The powers are equal, so compare the coefficients: $4.9 > 4.5$.
$4.9 \times 10^{4}$ is larger.

$310\,000 = 3.1 \times 10^{5}$ and $0.28 \times 10^{6} = 2.8 \times 10^{5}$
All the powers are $10^{5}$, so the coefficients set the order: $2.8 < 2.9 < 3.1$.
$0.28 \times 10^{6},\ 2.9 \times 10^{5},\ 310\,000$

The highest power wins: $10^{3} > 10^{2}$, even though $1.1$ is the smallest coefficient.
$1.1 \times 10^{3}$ is the largest.

$72 \times 10^{3} = 7.2 \times 10^{4}$
The powers are equal, so compare the coefficients: $7.2 > 6.9$.
$72 \times 10^{3}$ is larger.

development.question_text: Write a number in scientific notation that lies between $2 \times 10^{6}$ and $3 \times 10^{6}$.
development.solution_text:
The powers are equal, so any coefficient between $2$ and $3$ works, for example $2.2$.
$2.2 \times 10^{6}$

mastery.question_text: Zara says $8.7 \times 10^{-6}$ is larger than $2.3 \times 10^{-4}$ because $8.7$ is larger than $2.3$ and $6$ is larger than $4$. Explain why she is incorrect and state which number is larger.
mastery.solution_text:
The powers must be compared first, and for negative powers the one closer to zero is larger: $-4 > -6$.
$8.7 \times 10^{-6} = 0.000\,008\,7$ and $2.3 \times 10^{-4} = 0.000\,23$
$2.3 \times 10^{-4}$ is larger.

The $10^{6}$ numbers all come before $1.8 \times 10^{7}$; their coefficients order as $5.03 < 5.19 < 5.3$.
$5.03 \times 10^{6},\ 5.19 \times 10^{6},\ 5.3 \times 10^{6},\ 1.8 \times 10^{7}$
